english.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken equivalent when “actually” corrects or contrasts a claim.
Use this as the all-purpose choice when indeed means “actually” or “in fact.”
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that something is essentially or in effect the case.
Use this specifically to introduce an actual fact or correction, rather than to add emotional emphasis.

examples.english: Actually, I don't like spicy food.
examples.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 sik6 laat6

examples.english: Indeed, I haven't seen this movie.
examples.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 mei6 tai2 gwo3 ni1 tou3 hei3

examples.english: I’m effectively unavailable today, so I’ll go tomorrow.
examples.traditional: 其實我今日唔得閒，聽日先去啦。
examples.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 gam1 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4 ting1 jat6 sin1 heoi3 laa1

examples.english: Actually, I really don't know him.
examples.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 m4 sik1 keoi5
